claims.text: The Place du Tertre sits near the highest point of the Montmartre hill, at an altitude of 130 meters.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Before Montmartre was absorbed into Paris, this bustling area served as the main central square of the old independent village.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The name 'Tertre' likely refers to its elevated location, as the word simply translates to a small hill or mound.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: However, it could also be named after Guillaume Dutertre, a local man hired by the abbey all the way back in 1503.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Today it is famous worldwide for its many painters and café terraces, earning it the English nickname 'Artists' Square'.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Numerous artists still set up their easels here every single day to paint portraits for tourists and sell their original artwork.
claims.subject: self
